headline: A 2022 federal law bans making, selling, or distributing crib bumpers and inclined sleepers for infants.
what_it_does: The law makes it illegal to manufacture, sell, or distribute two types of baby sleep products. Crib bumpers are padded materials placed around the inside of a crib. Inclined sleepers are products for babies up to one year old that have a sleep surface tilted more than 10 degrees. Unpadded mesh crib liners are not covered by the ban.

who_it_affects.group: Manufacturers of crib bumpers and inclined sleepers
who_it_affects.how: They cannot make these products for sale in the United States under the ban.

who_it_affects.group: Retailers and distributors that sell baby sleep products
who_it_affects.how: They cannot sell or distribute crib bumpers or inclined sleepers covered by the ban.
They can no longer buy these covered products new from businesses, though the ban does not describe penalties for owning or using them.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on May 16, 2022.
